title: Gundam: Requiem for Vengeance
description: Mode design, combat and UI on an external-IP Fortnite game mode at Big Moxi Games.

items.label: External partnership
items.body: Authored and pitched high-level game-mode documentation for external IP partners, safeguarding brand alignment while protecting the core design pillars throughout development.

items.label: Combat & level design
items.body: Partnered with Level Design to optimise combat pacing and engagement vectors, keeping a balanced competitive sandbox within the structural limits of the map.

items.label: Cutscene development
items.body: Coordinated animation, art and engineering to implement an in-engine activation cutscene that bridged the narrative hook with live gameplay.

items.label: User interface
items.body: Worked with engineering on clean UI overlays and HUD feedback, maximising player orientation and macro-objective clarity during high-intensity combat.

blocks.text: Turning an engine limit into the core mechanic

blocks.html: The brief: design a competitive UEFN mode with controllable Gundam mechs that delivers a high-impact power fantasy without shattering sandbox balance.

The catch: at the time, UEFN restricted direct player control to native character avatars, so custom vehicle piloting was off the table. Rather than fight the bottleneck, I reframed it as the mode's primary competitive pacing hook.

blocks.caption: Players contest capture points; the leading team earns the mech and picks which preset zone to strike, turning a hard engine limit into a strategic hook.

items.label: Active engagement loops
items.body: Teams have to contest map objectives to earn mech activation, converting a technical limitation into a reason to keep fighting over the map.

items.label: Player-driven macro changes
items.body: Mech payloads target specific infrastructure nodes, so tactical decisions visibly alter the map geometry and the late-game lanes.

items.label: Immersive power fantasy
items.body: The automated sequence rewards the capture and sells the mech's scale and impact without custom controller mapping.

blocks.html: Happy to walk through the documentation, behaviour trees and tuning decisions behind this project.
